vo: Ancient Romans brushed their teeth with pee.
And not just any pee. They imported it from Portugal, because it was stronger.
Egyptians scrubbed with ox hoof ashes and crushed eggshells.
Greeks and Romans? Crushed bones and oyster shells.
And the first bristle toothbrush? Hair from a pig's neck.
But here's the crazy part. A lot of them had better teeth than you.
Skeletons from medieval Norway, a thousand years ago. Worn down, but almost no cavities.
Cavities started with the rich. Queen Elizabeth the First loved marzipan, and her teeth paid the price.
Then sugar got cheap, and everyone's teeth went downhill.
But not every ancient smile was perfect. One Stone Age group ate so many acorns, almost all of them had rotten teeth.
So yes, keep brushing. Toothpaste helps. But the real villain was always sugar.
Would you have survived Roman dentistry? Tell me in the comments.
